newsitem.title: UK: Labour's Wirral swing dwarfs pre-1992 by-elections.
newsitem.headline: Labour's Wirral swing dwarfs pre-1992 by-elections.

text.p: Voters in the Wirral South by-election have given the opposition Labour Party a far more ringing endorsement than it got in parliamentary by-elections which immediately preceded the 1992 general election.

The swing from the Conservatives to Labour in Thursday's by-election was 17.2 percent, which would have been modest had the contest occurred in mid-term, but is impressive in the dying days of a parliament.

Voting experts have calculated that at the upcoming general election, Labour will need a 4.3 percent swing in order to have an overall majority of the 659 members voters will elect to the House of Commons.
Labour won Wirral South by 7,888 votes, overturning a Conservative majority of 8,183.
Three by-elections held on November 7, 1991 proved the last such contests before the Conservatives gained a narrow election general election victory on April 9, 1992.

But only one of the three proved a close fight between the two main parties. In this by-election, at Langbaurgh in North Yorkshire, Labour won the seat from the Conservatives by 1,975 votes, but achieved a swing of only 3.6 percent.
The Conservatives won the seat back at the general election with a majority of 1,564.

The other two by-elections were Kincardine and Deeside in Scotland, which was won by the Liberal Democrats from the Conservatives on an 11.4 percent swing, and Hemsworth, a safe Labour seat in Yorkshire, which the party duly retained.
The Conservatives also regained the Kincardine seat at the 1992 general election. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
